editorial.headline: Wild Plant Propagation Is Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01302 covers the propagation of wild plants, with national PMA access up to 100% and no Bali moratorium block under the stated risk position.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01302 is a narrow but important activity: the propagation and breeding of wild plants. The Indonesian scope points to work that keeps plant reproduction going through practical propagation methods, including vegetative breeding from stem cuttings, plant pieces, and seedlings. In plain English, this is not a general farming label and not a broad trading category. It is for an operator whose registered activity is the controlled breeding or propagation of wild plant material so that the plants can continue to be developed and reproduced.

The record makes the scale picture unusually clean. This activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses. That means the classification is not reserved only for a large corporate operator, nor is it limited to a small local enterprise. A founder reading this should see it as a scale-flexible activity: the same activity description can sit across the stated business scales, provided the registered business is genuinely doing the propagation work described in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clear. At the national level, PMA is classified as TERBUKA, with a 100% foreign ownership ceiling. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so there is no need to soften the sentence: at the national level, this activity is open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That is the clean national baseline, and it matters because founders often confuse an open national classification with an automatically smooth local registration path.

For Bali, the honest reading is that this one is not blocked by the province’s PMA moratorium on the record provided. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, under the cited governor letter. But the Bali reason given here says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The result is a more practical conclusion than a blanket warning: KBLI 01302 is nationally open, can reach 100% foreign ownership, and is not marked as Bali-blocked in this record. The caveat is not a hidden prohibition; it is simply that the Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, which should be read exactly as stated rather than expanded into obligations the record does not give.
